summary: Verified the fix for the React 'destroy is not a function' TypeError on the AdminClients (/admin/clients) page. All 4 scenarios from the review request passed: (1) page renders CRM Clients heading + Add Client button + table (with empty state or data), (2) Add Client form saves via POST /api/admin/clients and refreshes the list, (3) Delete triggers window.confirm and removes the row via DELETE /api/admin/clients/:id, (4) Navigating away from /admin/clients to /admin/buyers does NOT throw the destroy-is-not-a-function error on unmount. Zero page errors and zero console errors captured during the full flow.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The AdminClients useEffect(load, []) -> useEffect(()=>{load();}, []) fix on App.js line 645 is confirmed working. No 'destroy is not a function' errors on mount, action, or unmount. If a similar useEffect(promiseReturningFn, []) pattern is added elsewhere, watch for the same regression (AdminDash line 612 uses a proper arrow already; AdminList line 632 uses proper arrow; AdminClients line 645 now uses proper arrow — all good).
rca of the issue: Root cause: React interprets any non-undefined return value from a useEffect callback as the cleanup function. When useEffect(load, []) was written with `load` being an arrow function that returns axios.get(...).then(...) (a Promise), on component unmount React tried to call promise() as a cleanup fn, causing 'TypeError: destroy is not a function'. Fix: wrap the call in an arrow that returns undefined — useEffect(()=>{ load(); }, []). Reproduction (before fix): login as admin, click CRM Clients, click any other sidebar link — error banner appeared. Mitigation: verified via Playwright — full mount → action → unmount cycle produces zero errors. Also confirmed no other admin components have this pattern.
